summary: Hotpath inspection and safe undo for config misalignment affecting tail latency
description:
Issue summary: CortexLabs reported a sudden increase in tail latency and intermittent 5xx errors after an optimizer configuration change was applied to their dedicated pool. The change included a mixed-precision quantization profile, aggressive batching windows, and enabling KV cache prefetch for low-latency paths.

Impact: Customer-facing inference for chat and generate endpoints experienced p95 latency jumps and a small but persistent 5xx rate, impacting a single high-traffic tenant. Traffic volume is production, dedicated pool. Customer has asked for a safe rollback procedure and guidance on how to profile the regression without causing customer-visible downtime.

Environment: prod-us-east dedicated pool (CortexLabs-reserved), affected model variants: llama-2-70b pinned -> mixed-quant profile; some requests hit a fallback redwood-rlhf-13b variant during overflow.

Ask: 1) Confirm root cause (config misalignment vs hardware noise). 2) Provide a minimal-risk rollback plan to restore stable p95 while preserving safety of long-lived sessions. 3) Suggest profiling steps to avoid reintroducing regression when re-enabling optimizations.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use CortexLabs tenant on prod-us-east with the current optimizer profile (mixed-quant + kv_prefetch enabled + aggressive batch policy).
2) Send a representative workload: bursty chat sessions with long context (avg 1800 tokens, tail 95th percentile episodes).
3) Observe p95 latency and any 5xx spikes in the first 10–30 minutes after traffic shift.
4) Compare to baseline with kv_prefetch disabled and quant profile set to fp16-only.
observed_behavior: p95 increased from ~120ms baseline to ~780ms for some requests; sustained 5xx rate ~0.8% (up from 0.05%). GPU utilization dropped on several nodes while CPU and mem pressure on host rose. Requests occasionally timed out during prefix cache warm-up windows.
expected_behavior: p95 should remain within SLO (<=200ms for this customer tier) and 5xx should stay <0.1% after configuration changes. Mixed-precision should reduce token cost without increasing tail latency for long-context sessions.
logs:
Grafana snapshot: https://grafana.redwood/cortexlabs/shot123 (p95 spike).
Edge logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:03Z ERROR serving-runtime: kv_prefetch miss, fallback path triggered.
Kernel selection logs: runtime/telemetry/2314 shows increased kernel fallback events at 14:11-14:18Z.
Slack thread: #support-cortexlabs (link in related_confluence_pages).
investigation_notes: Checked recent config rollout: deploy timestamp 2026-03-10T13:45Z, config bundle ID config-8472 changed quant profile and batching windows.
Observed a config diff: kv_prefetch switched from adaptive->always-on for CortexLabs tenant; batch window lowered from 40ms->12ms to favor throughput.
Telemetry shows repeated kernel fallback to conservative kernels when sequence length > 1024 — correlates with long-context requests.
GPU memory usage lower than expected; host-side CPU and page-faults increased consistent with frequent KV cache evictions during prefetch windows.

Hypothesis: combined effect of always-on kv_prefetch + tighter batching triggers cache churn and kernel fallback decisions on long-context requests, producing tail latency spikes. Quant profile likely exacerbates kernel incompatibility on some requests leading to fallback/heavier CPU paths.
No evidence of hardware degradation across nodes; replicas serving non-Cortex tenants show normal p95, pointing to tenant-specific config change as primary vector.
Related telemetry and stack traces attached in GitHub PR 2314 and config commit 7a8b3f4 for operator reference.

resolution_notes:
Workaround and rollback plan (agreed with customer):
1) Immediately enable traffic quarantine: route 20% of CortexLabs traffic to baseline profile (fp16 quant, kv_prefetch=adaptive) for 30 minutes and monitor p95/5xx.
2) If baseline bucket shows stable p95 and reduced errors, schedule progressive shift: 50% -> 80% -> 100% over 15-minute intervals.
3) Apply targeted config change on dedicated pool: revert kv_prefetch to adaptive and restore batching window to 40ms for tenant.
4) Revert quantization profile from mixed-quant to fp16-only for the tenant for the next 24 hours while engineering runs a safe repro and kernel compatibility test.
5) Drain and gracefully restart any replicas that reported kernel fallback before moving to full rollback completion.
6) Validate: confirm p95 <= 200ms and 5xx < 0.1% across 2 consecutive 30-minute windows in prod-us-east and eu-west.
7) Post-mortem actions: add canary checks for kernel fallback rates in optimizer rollout pipeline, improve preflight test to include long-context session simulation, and add a one-click escape hatch toggle for kv_prefetch at tenant granularity.

Follow-up: Assigned to Priya Kapoor for kernel compatibility investigation and to Luis Ortega for drafting a tenant-scoped rollback runbook. Customer accepted the staged rollback and reported improved p95 at 2026-03-12T17:20Z after stepwise reversion. Mark as awaiting closure after post-mortem published.
